The ninth and final season of the American television comedy ''[[The Office (American TV series)|The Office]]'' premiered on [[NBC]] on September 20, 2012, and concluded on May 16, 2013, consisting of 25 episodes. ''The Office'' is an American adaptation of the [[The Office (British TV series)|British comedy series]], and is presented in a [[mockumentary]] format, portraying the daily lives of office employees in the [[Scranton, Pennsylvania]] branch of the fictitious [[Dunder Mifflin|Dunder Mifflin Paper Company]]. The ninth season of ''The Office'' aired on Thursdays at 9:00&nbsp;p.m. ([[Eastern Time Zone (North America)|Eastern]]) in the United States, as part of the [[Comedy Night Done Right]] television block. It stars [[Rainn Wilson]], [[John Krasinski]], [[Jenna Fischer]], and [[Ed Helms]], with supporting performances from [[Catherine Tate]], [[Leslie David Baker]], [[Brian Baumgartner]], [[Creed Bratton]], [[Clark Duke]], [[Kate Flannery]], [[Mindy Kaling]], [[Ellie Kemper]], [[Angela Kinsey]], [[Jake Lacy]], [[Paul Lieberstein]], [[B. J. Novak]], [[Oscar Nunez]], [[Craig Robinson (actor)|Craig Robinson]], and [[Phyllis Smith]]. This is the second season not to star [[Steve Carell]] as lead character [[Michael Scott (The Office)|Michael Scott]], although he returned for a cameo appearance in [[Finale (The Office)|the series finale]].

The ninth season largely focuses on the relationship between [[Jim Halpert|Jim]] ([[John Krasinski]]) and [[Pam Beesly|Pam Halpert]] ([[Jenna Fischer]]). After Jim decides to follow his dream and start a sports marketing company in Philadelphia, Pam begins to worry about moving, and the couple's relationship experiences stress. Meanwhile, [[Andy Bernard]] ([[Ed Helms]]) abandons the office for a three-month boating trip, eventually quitting his job to pursue his dream of becoming a star, although he soon becomes famous for a [[viral video]]. [[Dwight Schrute]] ([[Rainn Wilson]]) is finally promoted to regional manager. The documentary airs, and a year later, the office members gather for Dwight and Angela's marriage and a final round of interviews.

Following the decline in ratings from the previous year, the ninth season of ''The Office'' managed to stabilize around 4 million viewers per episode. The series finale, however, was watched by over 5.69 million viewers, making it the highest-rated episode that the show had aired in over a year. The season ranked as the ninety-fourth most watched television series during the [[2012–13 United States network television schedule|2012–13 television year]] and saw a decrease in ratings from [[The Office (American season 8)|the previous season]]. Critical reception was moderately positive; although some critics took issue with certain aspects, such as the reveal of the in-series documentary crew, many argued that it was an improvement over the previous season. Others lauded the way the show was able to successfully wrap-up its story arcs. "Finale" was nominated for three awards at the [[65th Primetime Emmy Awards]], and won for [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Single-Camera Picture Editing for a Comedy Series|Outstanding Single-Camera Picture Editing for a Comedy Series]].

==Production==
The ninth season of the show was produced by [[Shine America]] and Deedle-Dee Productions, both in association with [[Universal Television]]. The show is based on the [[The Office (British TV series)|British comedy series of the same name]], which was created by [[Ricky Gervais]] and [[Stephen Merchant]] for the [[BBC]]. In addition, the two are executive producers on the show.<ref name="GreenLight">{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/media/2004/may/18/broadcasting.internationalnews |title=American Office Gets Green Light |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |first=Dave |last=Wood |date=May 18, 2004 |access-date=June 22, 2008}}</ref> On May 11, 2012, [[NBC]] renewed ''The Office'' for a ninth season.<ref name="season 9 renewal">{{cite web|url=https://www.tvguide.com/News/NBC-Renews-Office-Parks-Rec-Up-All-Night-1047375.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120515073154/http://www.tvguide.com/News/NBC-Renews-Office-Parks-Rec-Up-All-Night-1047375.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=May 15, 2012|title=NBC Renews ''The Office'', ''Parks and Recreation'', ''Up All Night'' and ''Whitney''|work=[[TV Guide]]|first=Robyn|last=Ross|date=May 11, 2012|access-date=May 11, 2012}}</ref> Series developer [[Greg Daniels]] returned as [[showrunner]] this season.<ref name="s9 showrunner">{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2012/05/15/business/media/networks-bank-on-comedies-for-2012-13-season.html |title=Comedies Lead the Way for the Next TV Season |author1=Carter, Bill |author2=Elliot, Stuart |date=May 14, 2012 |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=May 25, 2012}}</ref><ref name="b. j.">{{cite web|url=https://www.tvguide.com/News/BJ-Novak-Office-1049231.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120629095629/http://www.tvguide.com/News/BJ-Novak-Office-1049231.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-date=June 29, 2012 |title=B. J. Novak Takes an ''Office'' Breather |work=[[TV Guide]] |first=Michael |last=Schneider |date=June 27, 2012 |access-date=June 27, 2012}}</ref> Daniels stated that the season would feature more big [[Story arc|season arcs]], saying "I'll tell you that the last couple of years, I don't think we did any big arc-type things in the way that we used to in the beginning, I think the thing we're going to do is bring back a lot of arcs."<ref name="variety">{{cite web |url=http://weblogs.variety.com/thevote/2012/07/greg-daniels.html |title=Greg Daniels and the Future of 'The Office' |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |publisher=[[Penske Business Media]] |first=Jon |last=Weisman |date=July 5, 2012 |access-date=July 12, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120709092927/http://weblogs.variety.com/thevote/2012/07/greg-daniels.html |archive-date=July 9, 2012 }}</ref> [[Brent Forrester]], who had been a consulting producer and writer since the third season was promoted to executive producer, alongside new series writer [[Dan Sterling]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/office-executive-producers-season-9-327279|title='The Office' Adds Two EPs for Season 9|first=Lesley|last=Goldberg|work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=May 21, 2012|access-date=May 29, 2012}}</ref> 

In a conference call on August 21, 2012, Daniels announced that this would be the final season of the series. Daniels said, "This year feels like the last chance to really go out together and make an artistic ending for the show that pays off a lot of the stuff that matters most to fans."<ref name=EntertainmentWeekly /><ref name=bosspromise/> Daniels also said all the questions would be answered, such as who was behind the documentary, and why they had been filming it for so long, as well as the reveal of the Scranton Strangler.<ref name=EntertainmentWeekly /><ref name=bosspromise>{{cite web |url=https://www.tvline.com/news/the-office-ending-season-9-354994/ |title=The Office to End This Season, Show's Boss Promises 'All Questions Will Be Answered' |work=[[TVLine]] |first=Michael |last=Ausiello |date=August 21, 2012 |access-date=August 21, 2012}}</ref> A central point during the season was the romance between [[Erin Hannon]] ([[Ellie Kemper]]) and [[List of The Office (American TV series) characters|Pete Miller]] ([[Jake Lacy]]). According to Michael Ausiello of [[TVLine]], the nature of their relationship was heavily debated by the writers and producers; he noted that "the triangle [between Andy, Erin, and Pete] has stirred up a number of debates in the writers room, which tells me even they don't know at this point which guy Erin will choose."<ref name=tvlinespoiler>{{cite web|last=Ausiello|first=Michael|title=Ask Ausiello: Spoilers on Once Upon a Time, Bones, Office, Supernatural, HIMYM and More!|url=https://www.tvline.com/news/once-upon-a-time-spoilers-the-office-ask-ausiello-393417/|work=[[TVLine]]|access-date=January 5, 2013|date=January 3, 2013}}</ref> Daniels consulted with Kemper and asked for her input, as he felt she had the best understanding of Erin's characterization.<ref name="Stanhope1205">{{cite web|url=https://www.tvguide.com/News/Office-Ellie-Kemper-1057235.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121213052925/http://www.tvguide.com/News/Office-Ellie-Kemper-1057235.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 13, 2012|title=The Office's Ellie Kemper on Erin and Pete, a Very Dwight Christmas and Mindy Project|work=[[TV Guide]]|first=Kate|last=Stanhope|date=December 5, 2012|access-date=December 16, 2012}}</ref>

[[File:Dunder mifflin banner scranton.jpg|300px|thumb|[[Angela Kinsey]] and [[Rainn Wilson]] noted that the cast wanted to film an episode in [[Scranton, Pennsylvania]], where the series is set, although this never came to fruition.|alt=The image is of street banner that reads "Scranton" and Dunder Mifflin".]]
For the season, cast members John Krasinski, Jenna Fischer, Rainn Wilson, and Ed Helms were credited as producers.<ref name=EntertainmentWeekly /><ref name=bosspromise/> Krasinski also directed an episode.<ref>{{cite web|last=Baumgartner|first=Brian|title=John Krasinski Directing something funny in this weeks episode. Probably me|url=https://twitter.com/BBBaumgartner/status/248525200944152576|via=[[Twitter]]|access-date=September 25, 2012|date=September 12, 2012}}</ref> Guest directors for the season included [[Bryan Cranston]], who directed the episode "[[Work Bus]]",<ref name=bryan>{{cite magazine |url=http://insidetv.ew.com/2012/08/20/bryan-cranston-to-direct-the-office/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120820231524/http://insidetv.ew.com/2012/08/20/bryan-cranston-to-direct-the-office/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=August 20, 2012 |title=Bryan Cranston to Direct Episode of 'The Office' |magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]] |first=Dan |last=Snierson |date=August 20, 2012 |access-date=August 20, 2012}}</ref> and filmmaker [[Jon Favreau]], who directed the episode "[[Moving On (The Office)|Moving On]]".<ref>{{cite web|last=Ausiello|first=Michael|title=The Office Exclusive: Jon Favreau to Direct!|url=https://tvline.com/2013/01/02/the-office-season-9-spoilers-jon-favreau-directing/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130105011926/http://tvline.com/2013/01/02/the-office-season-9-spoilers-jon-favreau-directing/|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 5, 2013|work=[[TVLine]]|access-date=January 2, 2013|date=January 2, 2013}}</ref> Daniels directed the first episode, which he also wrote. Originally, the season was supposed to contain 24 episodes, which would have meant that the series aired exactly 200 episodes. However, the series' penultimate episode was elongated into 2 separate episodes, resulting in "[[Finale (The Office)|Finale]]"—which was announced previously as an hour-long special—being the 24th and 25th episodes of the season. This meant that the last part of "Finale" is the series' 201st episode.<ref name=25epsnot24>{{cite web|last=Tan|first=Jennie|title=The Office Season 9 Spoilers and News|url=https://www.officetally.com/the-office-season-9-spoilers-and-news|publisher=OfficeTally|access-date=March 5, 2013|date=March 5, 2013}}</ref> On March 19, 2013, the official ''Office'' fansite OfficeTally launched a campaign on [[Change.org]] to "super-size or extend" the finale; this campaign was motivated by a statement made by Daniels, in which he mentioned he would "beg" the studio to air a longer episode.<ref name=tallypet>{{cite web|last=Tan|first=Jennie|title=Petition to Supersize The Office Series Finale|url=https://www.officetally.com/petition-to-supersize-the-office-series-finale|publisher=OfficeTally|access-date=March 20, 2013|date=March 19, 2013}}</ref> On May 2, 2013, the petition amassed 20,000 signatures.<ref name=tallypet/> On May 7, NBC announced the series finale would be extended, and air in a 75-minute time slot.<ref name=55minutes>{{cite web|last=Ausiello|first=Michael|title=Scoop: NBC Expands The Office Series Finale|url=https://tvline.com/2013/05/07/the-office-series-finale-time-extra-15-minutes/|work=[[TVLine]]|access-date=May 7, 2013|date=May 7, 2013|archive-date=July 12, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210712101403/https://tvline.com/2013/05/07/the-office-series-finale-time-extra-15-minutes/|url-status=dead}}</ref> A one-hour retrospective of the series aired before the one-hour series finale on May 16.<ref>{{cite web|title=NBC, The CW Confirm Retrospective Specials Prior to "90210," "The Office" Finales|url=http://www.thefutoncritic.com/news/2013/04/05/nbc-the-cw-confirm-retrospective-specials-prior-to-90210-the-office-finales-674513/10274/|website=The Futon Critic|access-date=April 7, 2013|date=April 5, 2013}}</ref>

==Cast==
{{see also|List of The Office (American TV series) characters}}
''The Office'' employs an [[ensemble cast]]. Most of the main characters, and some supporting ones, are based on characters from the British version of ''The Office''. While these characters normally have the same attitudes and perceptions as their British counterparts, the roles have been redesigned to better fit the American show. The show is known for its large cast size, many of whom are known particularly for their [[improvisation]]al work.

===Main===
* [[Rainn Wilson]] as [[Dwight Schrute]], based upon [[Gareth Keenan]], who is the office's top-performing sales representative.
* [[John Krasinski]] as [[Jim Halpert]], a sales representative and prankster, who is based upon [[Tim Canterbury]], and is married to [[Pam Beesly|Pam Halpert]], the office administrator.
* [[Jenna Fischer]] as [[Pam Beesly|Pam Halpert]], who is based on [[Dawn Tinsley]], is shy, but is often a cohort with Jim in his pranks on Dwight. 
* [[Ed Helms]] as [[Andy Bernard]], the preppy manager and boastful Cornell alumnus whose love for [[a cappella]] music and awkward social skills generate mixed feelings from his employees.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://nbcumv.com/mediavillage/networks/nbcentertainment/theoffice|title=The Office Home|publisher=[[NBCUniversal]]|access-date=December 12, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111128222451/http://www.nbcumv.com/mediavillage/networks/nbcentertainment/theoffice|archive-date=November 28, 2011}}</ref>

===Casting===
Krasinski and Helms were expected to appear in fewer episodes in order to film several upcoming movies.<ref name="b. j."/> Helms was temporarily written out of the series with a storyline that saw his character travel to the Caribbean with his brother on a boat.<ref name=hangoverboat>{{cite web |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2012/11/09/the-office-the-boat-review |title=The Office: "The Boat" Review |author=White, Cindy |date=November 9, 2012 |work=[[IGN]] |publisher=[[News Corporation (1980–2013)|News Corporation]] |access-date= November 10, 2012}}</ref> As such, Helms made only a small appearance in "[[The Whale (The Office)|The Whale]]" and was absent from the following eight episodes. He returned in the episode "[[Couples Discount]]".<ref name=hangoverboat/> According to TVLine, he returned to work right before the show's Christmas break.<ref name=tvlinespoiler/> Krasinski ultimately continued to appear in every episode, but was frequently absent from the primary Scranton setting as part of a storyline that saw Jim begin a start-up business in Philadelphia. Additionally, Wilson was initially slated to appear in only 13 episodes before leaving for a planned Dwight-centric spin-off,<ref name="variety"/> but the spin-off was not picked up by NBC.<ref>{{cite web|last=Bricker|first=Tierney|title=Rainn Wilson's Office Spinoff, The Farm, Not Picked Up by NBC|url=https://www.eonline.com/news/358277/rainn-wilson-s-office-spinoff-the-farm-not-picked-up-by-nbc|publisher=[[E! News|E!]]|access-date=October 30, 2012|date=October 30, 2012}}</ref> Mindy Kaling and B. J. Novak have much lesser roles as [[Kelly Kapoor]] and [[Ryan Howard (The Office)|Ryan Howard]], respectively. [[File:Steve Carell November 2014.jpg|thumb|left|Former star [[Steve Carell]] reprised his role as [[Michael Scott (The Office)|Michael Scott]] in "[[Finale (The Office)|Finale]]".|alt=The image depicts a black-haired man; he is smiling at the camera.]]

Kinsey and Wilson also noted that the cast and crew could neither "confirm nor deny" but were "hoping" for a return of [[Steve Carell]] as [[Michael Scott (The Office)|Michael Scott]].<ref name=youtubekinwil/> In mid-December, Krasinski later revealed that he was optimistic about a return; in an interview with [[E!#E.21 Online|E! Online]] Krasinski said that the producers were supposedly "still trying to figure out [Carell's] schedule" and that the finale "just wouldn't be the same without him".<ref>{{cite web|title=Videos/Steve Carell Returning to "The Office"?|url=https://www.eonline.com/videos/199911/steve-carell-returning-to-the-office|publisher=[[E!#E.21 Online|E!]]|access-date=December 12, 2012}}</ref> However, NBC chairman [[Robert Greenblatt]] later admitted during an interview that while he is "hopeful", he does not think Carell will return; he noted that Carell was satisfied with his character's exit and did not want to tarnish it.<ref name="stevenot">{{cite web|last=Ausiello|first=Michael|title=Update: The Office Getting One-Hour Send-Off, NBC Boss Doubtful Steve Carell Will Return|url=https://www.tvline.com/news/the-office-series-finale-spoilers-steve-carell-393932/|work=[[TVLine]]|access-date=January 7, 2013|date=January 6, 2013}}</ref> On January 16, Daniels revealed that Carell would not appear in the finale in any capacity,<ref name="bigreveal" /> a decision that Carell later reiterated.<ref name=ibt>{{cite news|title=Will Michael Scott Return For 'The Office' Finale? Steve Carell Again Denies Possibility|url=https://www.ibtimes.com/will-michael-scott-return-office-finale-steve-carell-again-denies-possibility-1040898|access-date=January 26, 2013|newspaper=[[International Business Times]]|publisher=International Business Times, Inc.|date=January 26, 2013}}</ref> Three months later, however, the producers for ''The Office'' mounted "an 11th-hour effort last month" to get Carell to make a cameo in the show's final episode, according to TVLine.<ref name=tvlineapril/> Carell's personal representative confirmed that Carell was on the set for the final episode, but that he did not film any scenes. However, an anonymous source "close to the show" said "don't rule anything out".<ref name=tvlineapril>{{cite web|last=Ausiello|first=Michael|title=''The Office'' Mystery: Is Steve Carell Returning for the Series Finale After All?|url=https://www.tvline.com/casting-news/the-office-finale-steve-carell-returning-michael-scott-425581/|work=[[TVLine]]|access-date=April 17, 2013|date=April 17, 2013}}</ref> TVLine later reported on May 6, that Carell would appear in a cameo, although NBC declined to comment and Carell's representatives continued to deny the reports.<ref name=steveisback>{{cite web|last=Ausiello|first=Michael|title=Exclusive: Steve Carell Back for The Office Finale|url=https://www.tvline.com/casting-news/steve-carell-the-office-series-finale-430989/|work=[[TVLine]]|access-date=May 6, 2013|date=May 6, 2013}}</ref> Carell, however, did end up returning for the finale; his character, Michael Scott, becomes Dwight's best man at his wedding.<ref name=finaleepisode/><ref name=alanhitfix/> A month after the episode aired, Carell explained in an interview with TVLine that he "lied for months to the press, to almost everyone, really".<ref name=huffpostlie/> He noted that he "felt terribly for the cast and for [executive producer] Greg Daniels, because they all lied, too."<ref name=huffpostlie/> Krasinski, on the other hand, explained that "It was so thrilling. We all just flat-out lied … It was just one of those things that we all vowed and had to protect".<ref name=huffpostlie>{{cite web|title=Steve Carell On 'The Office' Finale: 'I Lied For Months'|url=https://www.huffingtonpost.com/2013/06/18/steve-carell-the-office-finale_n_3460924.html|publisher=[[Huffington Post|Huffpost TV]]|access-date=July 5, 2013|date=June 18, 2013}}</ref>

{{multiple image|total_width=330|image1=Daviddenman.jpg|image2=Melora Hardin 2009.jpg|footer=Several former cast members returned for guest appearances, including [[David Denman]] (''left'') and [[Melora Hardin]] (''right'').|alt1=A brown-haired man wearing a black shirt|alt2=A blond-haired woman smiling at the camera}}

In addition to Carell, the season also saw the return of several "veteran cast members".<ref>{{cite news|last=Sherrow|first=Rita|title=Last Season of 'The Office' Starts Thursday|url=http://www.tulsaworld.com/scene/article.aspx?subjectid=275&articleid=20120916_275_D3_CUTLIN782740|newspaper=[[Tulsa World]]|access-date=September 16, 2012|date=September 16, 2012}}</ref> ==Reception==
===Ratings===

{{image frame
|content={{#chart:OfficeUS9ratings.chart}}
|width = 500
|caption = Ratings for each episode of ''The Office'' that aired this season.{{ref|cite|i}}
}}

The season aired on Thursdays at 9:00&nbsp;p.m., as part of the [[Comedy Night Done Right]] programming block.<ref>{{cite web|last=Gorman|first=Bill|title=Fall 2012 TV Schedule Night by Night: Thursday|url=http://tvbythenumbers.zap2it.com/2012/05/17/fall-2012-night-by-night-thursday/134742/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120517161112/http://tvbythenumbers.zap2it.com/2012/05/17/fall-2012-night-by-night-thursday/134742/|url-status=dead|archive-date=May 17, 2012|work=[[TV by the Numbers]]|publisher=[[Zap2it]]|access-date=June 6, 2012|date=May 17, 2012}}</ref>  The season premiere, "[[New Guys]]" received a 2.1/6 percent share in the Nielsen ratings among viewers aged 18 to 49, meaning that 2.1 percent of viewers aged 18 to 49 watched the episode, and 6 percent of viewers watching television at the time watched the episode.<ref name=newguysrating/> The episode was viewed by 4.28 million viewers and became the lowest-rated season premiere for the series.<ref name=newguysrating/><ref name=ew2/> In addition, it marked a 46 percent drop in viewership from the season eight premiere "[[The List (The Office)|The List]]".<ref name=ew2>{{cite magazine|last=Hibberd|first=James|title=NBC Comedy Ratings Crash: 'The Office,' 'Parks' Return Lower|url=http://insidetv.ew.com/2012/09/21/office-parks-return/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120922114651/http://insidetv.ew.com/2012/09/21/office-parks-return/|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 22, 2012|magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]|access-date=September 21, 2012|date=September 21, 2012}}</ref> For the first sixteen episodes, the series was able to maintain roughly 4 million viewers. However, starting with the seventeenth episode "The Farm", ratings began to drop below this threshold.<ref name=farmratings/> The series hit an all-time low with the twentieth episode, "Paper Airplane", which was viewed by only 3.25 million viewers, and received a 1.7 rating/5 percent share.<ref name=paperairplaneratings/> The series finale was viewed by 5.69 million viewers and received a 3.0 rating among adults between the ages of 18 and 49.<ref name="2013finaleratings"/> This made it the highest-rated episode of the season; it also marked an increase in the [[Free Family Portrait Studio|previous season finale]], which garnered only 4.49 million viewers.<ref name="2013finaleratings"/><ref name=freefamily>{{cite web|last=Kondolojy|first=Amanda|title=Thursday Final Ratings: 'Big Bang Theory', 'Idol', 'Vampire Diaries', 'Office', 'Secret Circle', 'Grey's' Adjusted Up; 'Touch', 'Scandal' Adjusted Down|url=http://tvbythenumbers.zap2it.com/2012/05/11/thursday-final-ratings-big-bang-theory-idol-vampire-diaries-office-secret-circle-greys-adjusted-up-touch-scandal-adjusted-down/133458/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120513200626/http://tvbythenumbers.zap2it.com/2012/05/11/thursday-final-ratings-big-bang-theory-idol-vampire-diaries-office-secret-circle-greys-adjusted-up-touch-scandal-adjusted-down/133458/|url-status=dead|archive-date=May 13, 2012|work=[[TV by the Numbers]]|publisher=[[Zap2it]]|access-date=May 11, 2012|date=May 11, 2012}}</ref> "Finale" was the most watched episode of ''The Office'' since the eighth season episode "[[Pool Party (The Office)|Pool Party]]", but ranked as the third-least watched finale of the series, following the eighth- and [[The Office (American season 1)|first-season]] finales.<ref name=freefamily/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://tvbythenumbers.zap2it.com/2012/01/20/thursday-final-ratings-big-bang-theory-tops-american-idol-1st-half-hour-office-mentalist-greys-adj-up-person-rob-parks-adj-down/117089/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120123011608/http://tvbythenumbers.zap2it.com/2012/01/20/thursday-final-ratings-big-bang-theory-tops-american-idol-1st-half-hour-office-mentalist-greys-adj-up-person-rob-parks-adj-down/117089/|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 23, 2012|title=Thursday Final Ratings: 'Big Bang Theory' Tops 'American Idol' 1st Half Hour; 'Office,' 'Mentalist,' 'Grey's' Adj. Up; 'Person,' 'Rob,' 'Parks' Adj. Down|work=[[TV by the Numbers]]|publisher=[[Zap2it]]|last=Gorman|first=Bill|date=January 20, 2012|access-date=January 21, 2012}}</ref><ref name=hotpressrelease>{{cite press release |title=May 3, 2005 Press Release ("Hot Girl")|url= http://www.nbcumv.com/release_detail.nbc/entertainment-20050503000000-ahotmondaywithm.html |publisher=NBC|date=February 27, 2007|access-date=January 24, 2012}}{{dead link|date=June 2020|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} [https://www.officetally.com/the-office-nielsen-ratings/4 Alt URL]</ref>

By this season, ''The Office'' was no longer NBC's highest-rated scripted comedy series (having been surpassed by ''[[Go On (TV series)|Go On]]''),<ref name="adprices">{{cite web|last=Crupi|first=Anthony|title=Ads for The Office Finale Could Go for $400,000|url=http://www.adweek.com/news/television/long-goodbye-nbc-sets-premium-rates-super-sized-office-finale-149270|work=[[Adweek]]|access-date=May 13, 2013|date=May 7, 2013}}</ref><ref name="season9" /> it still often ranked as the highest-rated scripted NBC series on Thursday nights.{{ref|cite|i}} Rainn Wilson argued that the show's lower ratings were a combination of the overall trend in lower television ratings in 2012, as well as the fact that "NBC didn't promote [the series] one bit".<ref name="ama">{{cite web|last=Wilson|first=Rainn|title=IAM Rainn Wilson – Dwight From the Office and the Founder of SoulPancake – AMA!|url=https://www.reddit.com/r/IAmA/comments/11isz9/iam_rainn_wilson_dwight_from_the_office_and_the/|work=Reddit AMA|publisher=[[Reddit.com]]|access-date=October 20, 2012|date=October 16, 2012}}</ref> NBC increased their usual ad-price by 200 percent for the finale, asking for $400,000 per commercial. This was largely due to the anticipated increase in viewership that the finale would bring.<ref name="adprices" />

The season ranked as the ninety-fourth most watched television series during the [[2012–13 United States network television schedule|2012–13 season]], with an average of 5.061 million viewers.<ref name="season9">{{cite web|last=Bibel|first=Sara|title=Complete List Of 2012-13 Season TV Show Viewership: 'Sunday Night Football' Tops, Followed By 'NCIS,' 'The Big Bang Theory' & 'NCIS: Los Angeles'|url=http://tvbythenumbers.zap2it.com/2013/05/29/complete-list-of-2012-13-season-tv-show-viewership-sunday-night-football-tops-followed-by-ncis-the-big-bang-theory-ncis-los-angeles/184781/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130607112820/http://tvbythenumbers.zap2it.com/2013/05/29/complete-list-of-2012-13-season-tv-show-viewership-sunday-night-football-tops-followed-by-ncis-the-big-bang-theory-ncis-los-angeles/184781/|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 7, 2013|work=[[TV by the Numbers]]|publisher=[[Zap2it]]|access-date=May 29, 2013|date=May 29, 2013}}</ref> The season also tied with the [[CBS]] series ''[[Rules of Engagement (TV series)|Rules of Engagement]]'' and the [[Fox Broadcasting Company|Fox]] series ''[[American Dad!]]'' to be the forty-third most watched television series in the 18- to 49-year-old demographic. In this category, the show received a 2.6 rating. This meant that, on average, the season was viewed by 2.6 percent of all 18- to 49-year-olds. It was viewed by 3.32 million in this demographic.<ref>{{cite web|last=Bibel|first=Sara|title=Complete List Of 2012-13 Season TV Show Ratings: 'Sunday Night Football' Tops, Followed By 'The Big Bang Theory,' 'The Voice' & 'Modern Family'|url=http://tvbythenumbers.zap2it.com/2013/05/29/complete-list-of-2012-13-season-tv-show-ratings-sunday-night-football-tops-followed-by-the-big-bang-theory-the-voice-modern-family/184774/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130607112816/http://tvbythenumbers.zap2it.com/2013/05/29/complete-list-of-2012-13-season-tv-show-ratings-sunday-night-football-tops-followed-by-the-big-bang-theory-the-voice-modern-family/184774/|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 7, 2013|work=[[TV by the Numbers]]|publisher=[[Zap2it]]|access-date=May 29, 2013|date=May 29, 2013}}</ref> In terms of viewers, the ninth season ranked as the lowest-rated season of ''The Office'', although it beat the first season's ranking, which was the 102nd most watched program for the [[2004–05 United States network television schedule|2004–05 year]].<ref name="season9"/><ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/thr/television/feature_display.jsp?vnu_content_id=1000937471|title=Final audience and ratings figures for 2004-05|magazine=The Hollywood Reporter|access-date=September 30, 2008 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080423054904/http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/hr/search/article_display.jsp?vnu_content_id=1000937471 |archive-date=April 23, 2008 }}</ref>

===Critical response===
The ninth season of ''The Office'' received moderately positive reviews from television critics.<ref name=ibt/><ref name=meta/> Based on seven critiques, review aggregation website [[Metacritic]] gave the ninth season of the show a 64 out of 100 rating, which denotes "generally favorable" reviews.<ref name=meta>{{cite web|title=The Office: Season 9|url=https://www.metacritic.com/tv/the-office/season-9|publisher=[[Metacritic]]|access-date=December 19, 2012}}</ref> Entertainment website [[Holy Moly]] named the series one of the best shows during the 2012–13 season, writing that "this final season of ''The Office'' has been great" largely due to the fact that "every single relationship in the show rings true with the audience."<ref name=moly>{{cite web|last=Day-Preston|first=Becca|title=Best TV of 2012|url=http://www.holymoly.com/tv/blog/best-tv-2012-breaking-bad-game-thrones-girls-great-british-bake65468|work=[[Holy Moly]]|publisher=Holy Moly Entertainment Ltd|access-date=January 3, 2013|date=December 21, 2012}}</ref> Michael Tedder of ''[[Vulture (blog)|Vulture]]'' commented that he was "willing to call it the fourth best season of the show overall, which is by no means faint praise."<ref name=vulturefinale/> He explained that this was largely due to the fact that the "final season was a chance to see how everyone else would end up".<ref name=vulturefinale>{{cite web|last=Tedder|first=Michael|title=''The Office'' Finale Recap: That's All She Said|url=https://www.vulture.com/2013/05/office-finale-recap-thats-all-she-said.html|work=[[Vulture (blog)|Vulture]]|publisher=New York Media, LLC|access-date=May 18, 2013|date=May 17, 2013}}</ref> [[Emily St. James]] of ''[[The A.V. Club]]'' wrote that "the tension between Jim and Pam in the final season ended up being highly controversial for a number of reasons&nbsp;... but it also provided the most hopeful moments of the series' final stretch" (although she did note that it was clear that the writers had "blatantly" set up the drama).<ref name=avclubgreatest/> She concluded that the finale was able to successfully return the series "to what had always been its heart—to have true fulfillment".<ref name=avclubgreatest>{{cite web|last=St. James|first=Emily|title=How ''The Office'' Became One of the Greatest Television Series About the American Dream|url=https://www.avclub.com/how-the-office-became-one-of-the-greatest-television-se-1798238166|work=[[The A.V. Club]]|access-date=December 9, 2021|date=May 17, 2013}}</ref> Roth Cornet of [[IGN]] awarded the season an 8.5 out of 10, denoting a "great" year.<ref name=ignseasonreview/> She felt that the character growth in the final few episodes was particularly well executed, and the last stretch of the season helped raise it after a rocky start; ultimately, she felt that the writers were able to craft the proper ending for the show. She was, however, critical of Andy's characterization, noting that he was merely used as a plot device when convenient.<ref name=ignseasonreview>{{cite web|last=Cornet|first=Roth|title=The Office: Season 9 Review|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2013/05/22/the-office-season-9-review|work=[[IGN]]|publisher=[[News Corporation (1980–2013)|News Corporation]]|access-date=May 23, 2013|date=May 22, 2013}}</ref> Many critics argued that the season was an improvement, in both writing and humor, over the previous season.<ref name=moly/><ref>{{cite news|last=Owen|first=Rob|title='The Office' is Back&nbsp;– And Better|url=http://communityvoices.sites.post-gazette.com/index.php/arts-entertainment-living/tuned-in-journal/34239-the-office-is-back-and-better|access-date=September 20, 2012|newspaper=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]]|publisher=[[Block Communications]]|date=September 20, 2012|archive-date=October 8, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121008073053/http://communityvoices.sites.post-gazette.com/index.php/arts-entertainment-living/tuned-in-journal/34239-the-office-is-back-and-better|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|last=Tucker|first=Ken|title='The Office' Season Premiere Review: Now That's the Way to Start a Season|url= https://ew.com/article/2012/09/20/the-office-season-9-premiere/|magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]|access-date=December 9, 2021|date=September 20, 2012}}</ref>

Several specific episodes received praise. Andrea Reiher of [[Zap2it]] named "Dwight Christmas" the best comedy TV episode of 2012. She wrote that the episode "was not only funny but had a huge nostalgia factor", and continued the show's trend of strong Christmas episodes.<ref name=best/> Reiher also praised the episode's two subplots, writing that "drunk Darryl and ''Die Hard''" helped produce "a classic episode of ''The Office'' that brought back the warm and fuzzy feelings of the early seasons of the show."<ref name=best>{{cite web|last=Reiher |first=Andrea |title=The Best TV Episodes of 2012: 'The Good Wife,' 'The Office' and 'Big Brother' |url=http://blog.zap2it.com/frominsidethebox/2013/01/the-best-tv-episodes-of-2012-the-good-wife-the-office-and-big-brother.html |work=[[Zap2it]] |publisher=[[Tribune Media Services]] |access-date=January 3, 2013 |date=January 2, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130105172715/http://blog.zap2it.com/frominsidethebox/2013/01/the-best-tv-episodes-of-2012-the-good-wife-the-office-and-big-brother.html |archive-date=January 5, 2013 }}</ref> The season's penultimate entry, "[[A.A.R.M.]]", received a glowing response from many critics.<ref name=hitfixaarm/><ref name=tvwpoaarm>{{cite web|last=Giant |first=M. |title=A.A.R.M |url=http://www.televisionwithoutpity.com/show/the-office/aarm-9x22.php?page=11 |work=[[Television Without Pity]] |access-date=May 10, 2013 |date=May 10, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140329105335/http://www.televisionwithoutpity.com/show/the-office/aarm-9x22/11/ |archive-date=March 29, 2014 }}</ref><ref name=eonlineaarm>{{cite web|last=Mullins|first=Jenna|title=The Office Recap: An Engagement, a Dunder Mifflin Farewell and the Jim-Pam Tribute That Left Us in Tears|url=https://www.eonline.com/news/416959/the-office-recap-an-engagement-a-dunder-mifflin-farewell-and-the-jim-pam-tribute-that-left-us-in-tears|publisher=[[E!#E! Online|E!]]|access-date=May 11, 2013|date=May 10, 2013}}</ref><ref name=ignaarm>{{cite web|last=Cornet|first=Roth|title=The Office: A.A.R.M. Review|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2013/05/10/the-office-aarm-review|work=[[IGN]]|access-date=May 10, 2013|date=May 10, 2013}}</ref> [[Alan Sepinwall]] of [[HitFix]] wrote that the episode was "surprisingly&nbsp;... terrific in most areas."<ref name=hitfixaarm>{{cite news|last=Sepinwall|first=Alan|title=Review: 'The Office' – 'A.A.R.M.': The Teapot Dome Affair|url= https://uproxx.com/sepinwall/review-the-office-a-a-r-m-the-teapot-dome-affair/|work=[[Uproxx]]|access-date=December 9, 2021|date=May 9, 2013}}</ref> Roth Cornet of [[IGN]] noted that "The interplay between Jim, Dwight, and Pam has been the core of the series since Michael Scott's departure, and it was good to see the trio front and center once again as ''The Office'' comes to a close."<ref name=ignaarm/> The series finale, in particular, was praised by critics. Sepinwall called it "a tremendously satisfying conclusion to a show that could make us gasp with laughter, but that could also make us cry or smile".<ref name=alanhitfix/> Cornet wrote that it "was a strong hour of television [and] the finale shone and delivered on all of its promise."<ref>{{cite web|last=Cornet|first=Roth|title='Finale' Review|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2013/05/17/the-office-finale-review|work=[[IGN]]|publisher=[[News Corporation (1980–2013)|News Corporation]]|access-date=May 17, 2013|date=May 17, 2013}}</ref> Nick Campbell of [[TV.com]] wrote that the episode was "just right" for the series.<ref>{{cite web|last=Campbell|first=Nick|title=''The Office'' Series Finale Review: That'll Do, Show. That'll Do|url=http://www.tv.com/news/the-office-series-finale-review-thatll-do-show-thatll-do-136881069650/|work=[[TV.com]]|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|access-date=May 17, 2013|date=May 17, 2013|archive-date=June 7, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130607111342/http://www.tv.com/news/the-office-series-finale-review-thatll-do-show-thatll-do-136881069650/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Other episodes were not received as positively. "Lice", for instance, was called "terrible" by Campbell, as well as the "epitome of filler" by Brett Davinger of ''The California Literary Review''.<ref>{{cite web|last=Campbell|first=Nick|title=The Office: 'Lice' Review: I'd Rather Have Actual Lice|url=http://www.tv.com/news/the-office-lice-review-id-rather-have-actual-lice-30380/|work=[[TV.com]]|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|access-date=January 12, 2013|date=January 11, 2013|archive-date=January 13, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130113045413/http://www.tv.com/news/the-office-lice-review-id-rather-have-actual-lice-30380/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Davinger|first=Brett|title=The Office Recap: 'Lice' (Season 9, Episode 10)|url=http://calitreview.com/34348|work=The California Literary Review|access-date=January 12, 2013|archive-date=January 14, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130114004823/http://calitreview.com/34348|url-status=dead}}</ref> "The Farm" was largely derided due to its uneven nature, and the broad humor that it used.<ref name="tv.com">{{cite web |author=Campbell, Nick |url=http://www.tv.com/news/the-officenbspthe-farm-review-try-not-to-laugh-when-we-say-backdoor-136335502551/ |title=The Office 'The Farm' Review: Try Not to Laugh When We Say "Backdoor" |work=[[TV.com]]|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]  |date=March 15, 2013 |access-date=March 30, 2013 |archive-date=March 19, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130319060024/http://www.tv.com/news/the-officenbspthe-farm-review-try-not-to-laugh-when-we-say-backdoor-136335502551/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="ign">{{cite web|author=Cornet, Roth |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2013/03/15/the-office-the-farm-review |title=The Office: "The Farm" Review |work=[[IGN]]|publisher=[[News Corporation (1980–2013)|News Corporation]] |date=March 15, 2013 |access-date=March 25, 2013}}</ref>

The reveal of the in-series documentary crew in "Customer Loyalty" received large amounts of critical attention. [[E! Online]] named the reveal one of the "Best TV Moments of the Week".<ref>{{cite web|last=Mullins|first=Jenna|title=Best TV Moments of the Week: The Office, Glee, American Idol and More|url=https://www.eonline.com/news/381988/best-tv-moments-of-the-week-the-office-glee-american-idol-and-more|publisher=E!|access-date=January 26, 2013|date=January 25, 2013}}</ref> Verne Gay of ''[[Newsday]]'' called the scene a "historic" moment for the show.<ref>{{cite web|last=Gay|first=Verne|title='The Office': Meet the Documentary Crew|url=https://www.newsday.com/entertainment/tv/the-office-meet-the-documentary-crew-d70444|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130128103655/http://www.newsday.com/entertainment/tv/tv-zone-1.811968/the-office-meet-the-documentary-crew-1.4508655|url-status=live|archive-date=January 28, 2013|work=[[Newsday]]|publisher=[[Cablevision]]|access-date=January 25, 2013|date=January 25, 2013}}</ref> Conversely, Myles McNutt of ''The A.V. Club'' wrote an article that argued that the mockumentary format made the camera "an audience surrogate", and that by revealing the documentary crew, "the audience no longer felt welcome".<ref name=pitfalls>{{cite web|last=McNutt|first=Myles|title=The Office Shows the Pitfalls of Fake Reality Becoming "Real"|url=https://www.avclub.com/the-office-shows-the-pitfalls-of-fake-reality-becoming-1798236235|work=[[The A.V. Club]]|access-date=December 9, 2021|date=February 11, 2013}}</ref> The subplot involving Brian (played by [[Chris Diamantopoulos]]), a boom mic operator for the in-series documentary, was met with mostly negative reviews. Michael Tedder of ''Vulture'' called it "the least interesting way this camera crew reveal could have gone".<ref name=vulture>{{cite web|last=Tedder|first=Michael|title=The Office Recap: Life of Brian|url=https://www.vulture.com/2013/02/office-recap-season-9-episode-13-14.html|work=[[Vulture (blog)|Vulture]]|publisher=New York Media, LLC|access-date=February 1, 2013|date=February 1, 2013}}</ref> Dan Forcella of TV Fanatic criticized the reintroduction of the character in the episode "Promos", noting that his reappearance felt "forced".<ref>{{cite web|last=Forcella|first=Dan|title=The Office Review: They Filmed Everything|url=http://origin.tvfanatic.com/2013/04/the-office-review-they-filmed-everything/|publisher=TV Fanatic|access-date=April 13, 2013|date=April 5, 2013|archive-date=May 3, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130503152947/http://origin.tvfanatic.com/2013/04/the-office-review-they-filmed-everything/|url-status=dead}}</ref> McNutt called it "an abandoned novelty".<ref name=pitfalls/> Daniels later revealed in an interview that the subplot was a [[red herring]] to keep viewers emotionally invested in Pam and Jim's story. He explained, "we never intended him to actually [interfere with Pam and Jim's marriage], but wanted people to worry about it so they would be engaged in the story."<ref>{{cite web|last=Cornet|first=Roth|title=The Office's Greg Daniels on the End of His Decade-Long Journey|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2013/05/11/the-offices-greg-daniels-on-the-end-of-his-decade-long-journey?page=2|work=[[IGN]]|publisher=[[News Corporation (1980–2013)|News Corporation]]|access-date=May 16, 2013|date=May 11, 2013}}</ref>

===Awards===
On December 12, 2012, the series was nominated for a [[Screen Actors Guild Award]] for [[Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by an Ensemble in a Comedy Series|Outstanding Performance by an Ensemble in a Comedy Series]], but lost to ''[[Modern Family]]''.<ref>{{cite web|title=Nominations Announced for the 19th Annual Screen Actors Guild Awards®|url=http://www.sagawards.org/media-pr/press-releases/nominations-announced-19th-annual-screen-actors-guild-awards®|work=SAGAwards.com|publisher=[[Screen Actors Guild]]|access-date=December 12, 2012|date=December 12, 2012|archive-date=May 28, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150528131000/http://www.sagawards.org/media-pr/press-releases/nominations-announced-19th-annual-screen-actors-guild-awards%C2%AE|url-status=dead}}</ref><!-- I assume this is for the season, since it mentions Lacey, Duke, and Tate as part of the ensemble, and doesn't include Woods. --><ref>{{cite web|last=Surette|first=Tim|title=The 2013 SAG Awards: Wins for Modern Family and Downton Abbey|url=http://www.tv.com/news/the-2013-sag-awards-wins-for-modern-family-and-downton-abbey-30494/|publisher=[[TV.com]]|access-date=January 28, 2013|date=January 28, 2013|archive-date=January 30, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130130120754/http://www.tv.com/news/the-2013-sag-awards-wins-for-modern-family-and-downton-abbey-30494/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Michael Scott's return was nominated and won the fan-voted "Best TV Moment" at the [[3rd Critics' Choice Television Awards]] on June 10, 2013.<ref>{{cite web|last=Richenthal|first=Matt|title=Critics' Choice Television Award Winners: TBBT, AHS and More!|url=http://www.tvfanatic.com/2013/06/critics-choice-television-award-winners-tbbt-ahs-and-more/|publisher=TV Fanatic|access-date=June 14, 2013|date=June 11, 2013}}</ref> Greg Daniels was nominated for a [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Writing for a Comedy Series]] at the [[65th Primetime Emmy Awards]] for "Finale".<ref name=emmysnews/> "Finale" was also nominated for an Outstanding Sound Mixing for a Comedy or Drama Series Emmy and an [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Single-Camera Picture Editing for a Comedy Series|Outstanding Single-Camera Picture Editing for a Comedy Series]] Emmy; [[David Rogers (film editor)|David Rogers]] and Claire Scanlon for "Finale" won the latter, marking the fifth win for ''The Office'' at the Emmys overall and the series' first win since 2009.<ref>{{cite web|last=Tan|first=Jennie|title=The Office Nominated for 4 Emmys|url=https://www.officetally.com/the-office-nominated-for-4-emmys|publisher=OfficeTally|access-date=July 19, 2013|date=July 18, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.emmys.com/shows/office |title=The Office |publisher=Emmys.com |access-date=July 22, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Andreeva|first=Nellie|title=HBO, 'Behind The Candelabra' Lead Creative Arts Emmy Awards; 'Undercover Boss', 'South Park', Tony Awards, Bob Newhart, Dan Bucatinsky, Melissa Leo, Carrie Preston, Heidi Klum & Tim Gunn Among|url=https://deadline.com/2013/09/creative-arts-emmy-awards-2013-winners-live-587432/|access-date=September 16, 2013|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|date=September 15, 2013}}</ref> Rogers and Scanlon also won an [[American Cinema Editors]] award for Best Edited Half-Hour Series for Television.<ref>{{cite web|title=64th Annual ACE Eddie Awards: 'Captain Phillips' Wins Drama Feature Prize; 'American Hustle' Top Comedy; 'Frozen' Wins Animation Trophy; 'Breaking Bad' & 'The Office' Take Top TV Prizes|url=https://deadline.com/2014/02/eddie-award-winners-2014-american-cinema-editors-awards-679543/|access-date=February 8, 2014|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|date=February 7, 2014}}</ref> In addition, the web documentary "The Office: The Farewells", which aired on NBC.com prior to the series' conclusion, was nominated for an Outstanding Special Class Program Creative Arts Emmy Award.<ref name=emmysnews>{{cite news|last=Elber|first=Lynn|title=Emmy nominations: 'The Office' Shut Out of Nominations in Major Categories, 'House of Cards' Makes History|url=http://thetimes-tribune.com/news/emmy-nominations-the-office-shut-out-of-nominations-in-major-categories-house-of-cards-makes-history-1.1522496|access-date=July 19, 2013|newspaper=[[The Times-Tribune (Scranton)|The Times-Tribune]]|date=July 18, 2013|publisher=[[Times-Shamrock Communications]]}}</ref>

==Home media release==
The ninth season of ''The Office'' was released by Universal Studios Home Entertainment as a five-disc set on both [[DVD region code#Region codes and countries|Region 1]] DVD and a [[Blu-ray Disc|Region A]] Blu-ray on September 3, 2013.<ref name=amazon.comdvd>{{cite web|title=The Office: Season Nine [Blu-ray] (2013)|website=Amazon |url=https://www.amazon.com/dp/B009LDD4I2/|access-date=September 4, 2013}}</ref> The set contains all 25 episodes of the season presented in a 1.78:1 widescreen aspect ratio with Dolby Digital audio and optional English and Spanish subtitles. The release also includes a variety of deleted scenes, 2003 casting tapes, "The Office: A Look Back" Retrospective featurette, a table read of the "Finale" script, the "Autotune Andy" music video. The Blu-ray release also contains an exclusive "Behind-the-Scenes Panel Discussion".<ref name="DVD4">{{cite AV media notes |title=The Office: The Complete Ninth Season |others=[[Greg Daniels]], et al |type=insert |publisher=[[NBC]]}}</ref>
